summary: Every allocation must influence its team average, and the contract can require all arbitrary employee identifiers to be returned in sorted order.

optimality.argument: All n rows may qualify and must then be ordered by arbitrary identifiers, requiring comparison sorting in Omega(n log n); one window aggregation plus the final sort achieves O(n log n).

replacement_checks.evidence: A legal result may contain all n arbitrary employee identifiers in mandated ascending order.
One joined window calculation annotates every row, and a final comparison sort orders qualifying rows.
Cases cover the official sample, equality exclusion, singleton teams, fractional averages, multiple teams, and identifier order.
